sources.title: Configure permissions: Read(./.env) matches reading the .env file in the current directory; Read and Edit deny rules apply to Claude's built-in file tools, to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash such as cat, head, tail, sed, tee, and to redirections; they don't apply to arbitrary subprocesses that read files indirectly, like a Python or Node script that opens files itself; for OS-level enforcement enable the sandbox; an allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule

layout.description: Real run, recorded on Nov 2, 2026 with Claude Code 2.1.309 (model claude-haiku-5-5). Four runs in a test folder with made-up values, each one twice, with the same result: Without a rule, Claude read .env. With the deny rule Read(./.env), reading was denied, and so was an explicitly allowed cat. An allowed Node script that opens the file itself still printed the key. That matches the docs.
layout.companion_text: Base command per run: claude -p "<prompt>" --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --tools Read,Bash,Grep,Glob. Run 3 also --allowedTools "Bash(cat *)", run 4 --allowedTools "Bash(node show-env.js)". Rule in .claude/settings.json: {"permissions": {"deny": ["Read(./.env)"]}}. Paths shortened in the frame (test folder = .). Behaviour can change with version and model. Not an official Anthropic channel.

beats.spoken: Can one single rule keep Claude Code away from your .env file? I tested it in four real runs.
The test folder holds a .env file with made-up values, plus a small Node script that reads the file by itself.
The block is this one line in settings.json. According to the docs it also covers cat, but not scripts that open files themselves.

data.quote: They don't apply to … a Python or Node script that opens files itself.
data.translation: Scripts that open files on their own are not covered.

beats.spoken: Run one, no rule yet. Claude started, read the file with the Read tool and named the value.
Run two, with the rule. The read was denied, and Claude wrote that it would not get around the restriction another way.
Run three. I allowed cat explicitly. The deny rule still won, and the command was denied.
Run four. This time I allowed the Node script. It opened the file itself, and the full key showed up in the answer.

Every run ran twice, with the same result. The rule blocks Claude's tools and commands like cat, but according to the docs not scripts that open files themselves. For a hard block, the docs point to the sandbox.

data.headline: 4 runs, twice each
data.note: A block for every program: the sandbox, per the docs.

beats.spoken: So only allow scripts when you know what they read. Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step.

data.statement: Only allow scripts when you know what they read.
